reviewers.summary: The passcode step reveals the seeded-user list without validating the passcode, and sign-in omits the required anti-forgery token. The named test explicitly expects that token to be absent.

findingList.message: The seeded-user picker is exposed before the passcode is validated, contrary to the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that the passcode is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users and displays the returned users without validating the passcode.
evidence.failureScenario: A visitor enters an incorrect nonempty passcode; if /api/auth/users returns the seeded users, the picker reveals their names and roles before a successful sign-in step (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

findingList.message: The sign-in request omits the anti-forgery token required on every state-changing request.

evidence.codePathTraced: signIn sends a state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in with only a Content-Type header and no anti-forgery token.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires the specified anti-forgery header, submitting the sign-in form omits it and the request is rejected (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

findingList.message: The test asserts the opposite of the anti-forgery requirement and cannot catch a missing sign-in token.

evidence.codePathTraced: The named test asserts that the sign-in request's X-CSRF-Token header is undefined, encoding the omission instead of checking the required anti-forgery token.
evidence.failureScenario: If the sign-in anti-forgery header is removed, this test still passes, so the issue's named-test criterion is not met.

reviewers.summary: The passcode step reveals the seeded-user roster before validating the passcode, and sign-in omits the required anti-forgery header. The tests also do not catch the premature picker.

findingList.message: The seeded-user picker is shown without validating the passcode, contrary to the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that passcode is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users and displays the result without validating the passcode.
evidence.failureScenario: A visitor enters an incorrect nonempty passcode and /api/auth/users returns the seeded users; the picker appears before a successful passcode step, exposing the roster (OWASP A01:2025).

findingList.message: The sign-in request omits the anti-forgery token required on every state-changing request.

evidence.codePathTraced: signIn sends a state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in with only a Content-Type header and no anti-forgery token.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires the specified anti-forgery header, submitting sign-in omits it and the server rejects the request (OWASP A01:2025).

findingList.message: The tests do not check that an incorrect passcode keeps the seeded-user picker hidden, as required by the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: The passcode-step test uses a nonempty passcode and expects users to appear; the wrong-passcode test reaches the picker and checks the message only after submitting sign-in.
evidence.failureScenario: If any nonempty passcode reveals the picker, the current tests still pass, so they do not verify the first acceptance criterion's requirement that users appear only after a successful passcode step.

reviewers.summary: The passcode is not validated before the seeded-user list is fetched, and the state-changing sign-in request omits the required anti-forgery header.

findingList.message: The seeded-user roster is exposed before passcode validation, contrary to the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: The passcode handler checks only that the field is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users and displays the response without sending or validating the passcode.
evidence.failureScenario: An unauthenticated visitor enters any nonempty value; if /api/auth/users returns the seeded users, the picker exposes their names and roles before the passcode is accepted (OWASP A01:2025).

findingList.message: The sign-in request omits the required anti-forgery header.

evidence.codePathTraced: The state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in sends only Content-Type; it does not include the anti-forgery token header required by the acceptance criterion.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires its cookie-bound anti-forgery header, submitting the sign-in form omits it and the server rejects the request (OWASP A01:2025).
